summary: This work proposes a decoherence-free subspace (DFS) encoded superconducting geometric logical $T$ gate using optimized composite pulse engineering to achieve fourth-order suppression of Rabi frequency, detuning, and residual inter-qubit crosstalk errors while inherently suppressing collective dephasing. Numerical simulations on tunable transmon circuits with parametric coupling show the two-loop optimized composite geometric $T$ gate achieves $>99.9\%$ fidelity over a wide error range, outperforming conventional composite geometric and dynamical $T$ gates.
motivation: Magic state distillation for high-fidelity $T$ gates requires prohibitive physical qubit overhead and complex measurement-feedback control; direct high-fidelity logical $T$ gate construction at the physical layer would reduce resource consumption and simplify fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.
method: Two target transmons in a 2D superconducting lattice are coupled via ac-driven tunable coupling ($g_{12}^{\prime} = J_1(\beta)g_{12}$), with information encoded in the single-excitation DFS ($|10\rangle_{12} = |0\rangle_L$, $|01\rangle_{12} = |1\rangle_L$). The scheme integrates multi-loop optimized composite geometric trajectories on the Bloch sphere with unconstrained inter-loop angular separations ($p_1 = 1.0625\pi$ for two loops, $p_1 \approx 1.38\pi$ for three loops) that simultaneously suppress all three error channels along a single path.
result: With optimal modulation parameters ($\beta = 1.85$, $\Delta = 2\pi \times 462$ MHz) and energy relaxation $\kappa_- = 2\pi \times 2$ kHz, the logical OCGT gate reaches $99.79\%$ fidelity with leakage suppressed below $0.01\%$; it maintains $>99.9\%$ fidelity at $\kappa_- < 2\pi \times 1$ kHz over error amplitudes $\pm 2\pi \times 2$ MHz in Rabi, detuning, and crosstalk channels, significantly outperforming conventional geometric and dynamical $T$ gates.
